patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is the real Botan fix for this path: it changes `bigint_cnd_{add,sub}` to declare `word z[8] = { 0 };` and routes the scalar tail through `z[0]`. The fixed instrumented run still executes the same `sub_select_read -> abs_limb_read -> word_add_sink` path on the original PoC, but records `z_initialized_prefix_len=64`, `abs_limb_initialized_prefix_len=8`, and `x_initialized_prefix_len=8`, then exits clean.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code materialization of attacker-controlled state on the crashing path: the witness buffer is split into two BigInt operands `x` and `mod` that later drive the odd-modulus inversion routine.

Root cause. `bigint_cnd_sub()` uses stack buffer `z[8]` as the destination for the 8-word subtraction helper but does not initialize it in source, so later C++ reads stay poisoned under MSan when the result came from inline asm.
MemorySanitizer crash site. `word_add()` consumes the poisoned limb value propagated out of `bigint_cnd_sub()` and reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in the x86_64 asm-backed addition helper.

At `x[i+j] = CT::select(mask, z[j], x[i+j]);`, the first selected limb is read from a temporary `z` buffer whose initialized prefix is still 0 bytes across the 64-byte block on the crashing vulnerable execution.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `sub_select_read.z_buffer_bytes=64` and `sub_select_read.z_initialized_prefix_len=0` at the `CT::select` read.

nodes.description: At `const word z = word_add(~x[i], 0, &carry);`, `bigint_cnd_abs()` immediately reads the propagated first limb `x[0]` while 0 of its 8 bytes are initialized on the vulnerable execution.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `abs_limb_read.abs_limb_bytes=8` and `abs_limb_read.abs_limb_initialized_prefix_len=0` at the first `bigint_cnd_abs()` iteration.

edges.description: The same stack buffer allocated as `z` at the root declaration is the temporary buffer later read by the block-path `CT::select` statement.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `sub_tmp_decl.z_buffer_ptr == sub_select_read.z_buffer_ptr` for the crashing call.

edges.description: The first limb storage selected at `x[i+j]` in `bigint_cnd_sub()` is the same `x[0]` limb immediately read by the following `bigint_cnd_abs()` call.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `sub_select_read.selected_limb_ptr == abs_limb_read.abs_limb_ptr == 0x704000000080`.

edges.description: The complemented first-limb value `~x[0]` computed in `bigint_cnd_abs()` is passed unchanged as the `x` argument into the later `word_add()` sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `abs_limb_read.word_add_x_bits == word_add_sink.x_bits == 18446744073709551393`, and the fixed trace preserves the same equality for its first clean execution.
